title: WAMs and VLAs for Robot Learning | Cosmos Labs
summary: NVIDIA’s Cosmos Labs livestream lays out how World Action Models and vision-language-action models play different roles in robot foundation models, with WAMs modeling future observations and actions while VLAs connect perception, language, and control. It centers on Cosmos 3, which treats action as a native modality alongside video, and shows how Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID can imagine future observations while generating robot actions. The session is framed as a practical path for adapting and deploying these models with open Cosmos models, datasets, recipes, evaluation workflows, and serving resources.

extra.full_text: Building capable robot foundation models requires more than one approach. Vision-language-action (VLA) models and World Action Models (WAMs) - each offer different strengths for robot learning, planning, and control. In this livestream, NVIDIA researchers Danfei Xu US Moritz Benno Reuss CH Thomas Tian US will explore what World Action Models work, how they compare with modern Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and why many next-generation robot foundation models combine both approaches. You'll also see how NVIDIA Cosmos 3 treats action as a native modality, enabling robots to predict future observations while generating actions. We'll walk through how Cosmos 3 provides an open workflow for post-training, evaluation, and deployment using open models, datasets, recipes, and serving resources. Whether you're building manipulation policies, training robot foundation models, or exploring embodied AI, this livestream provides a practical understanding of where World Action Models fit into the future of robotics. What You'll Learn: - What World Action Models are and how they differ from and complement Vision-Language-Action models - The strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs of WAMs, VLAs, and emerging hybrid approaches - How Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID imagines future observations while generating robot actions - How NVIDIA Cosmos 3 represents action as a native modality alongside video - How to evaluate, post-train, and adapt Cosmos 3 using open models, datasets, recipes, and serving resources Have questions about how to post-train and deploy NVIDIA Cosmos 3? Drop them live — the NVIDIA team will answer them in real time. title: $ω$-0: A Latent Predictive World Action Model for Concurrent Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: $ω$-0 is a whole-body latent world-action model that maps language, visual observations, and proprioception directly into controller-compatible action latents for humanoids doing household tasks that require moving and manipulating at the same time. Instead of predicting future video, it learns compact future observation embeddings and uses diffusion to generate coordinated whole-body actions, with support for egocentric RGB, exocentric RGB, and exocentric depth inputs. The authors also introduce the 40+ hour $ω$-HOME dataset, and real-robot tests on 11 household tasks show one model producing smooth manipulate-while-moving behavior while outperforming imitation learning, VLA, humanoid, and world-action-model baselines.

extra.full_text: Humanoid household tasks often require concurrent loco-manipulation, where the robot must move, adjust posture, maintain balance, and manipulate objects as a single coordinated behavior. Yet existing humanoid policies typically decompose locomotion and manipulation, while recent world-action models remain either arm-centric or video-centered. We present $ω$-0, a latent predictive whole-body world-action model for real-world humanoid concurrent loco-manipulation. Given a language instruction, current visual observation, and robot proprioceptive state, $ω$-0 directly predicts controller-compatible whole-body action latents for real-robot execution. Rather than reconstructing future videos, $ω$-0 learns compact future observation embeddings as a lightweight predictive objective, coupling latent visual foresight with diffusion-based whole-body action generation. The model supports egocentric RGB, exocentric RGB, and exocentric depth inputs, and leverages controller-based simulation replay to ground human/public visual-motion priors into robot-executable action latents. We further collect $ω$-HOME, a 40+ hour real-world household humanoid dataset with synchronized multi-view observations, whole-body SMPL motions, robot states, and action latents. Real-world experiments on 11 household tasks demonstrate that a single $ω$-0 model can produce smooth manipulate-while-moving behaviors and consistently outperform representative imitation learning, VLA, humanoid, and WAM baselines.

title: GeniWorld: A Generalizable Interactive World Model for Robotic Manipulation via Visual Actions
summary: GeniWorld turns robot actions into spatially grounded visual action representations using URDF-based rendering, then feeds them into a pretrained video generative model to predict interactive manipulation rollouts. By separating robot embodiment kinematics from scene dynamics and coupling autoregressive video prediction with high-frequency kinematic control, it can support closed-loop interaction with policies or human teleoperators. Trained only on limited fixed-scene data, it generalizes zero-shot to randomized unseen environments and can be used both to evaluate policies under perturbations and to synthesize diverse trajectories that improve downstream robustness.

extra.full_text: Generalist robot policies exhibit strong capabilities, but their robustness in complex and unseen environments remains limited. Scaling robot learning and evaluation in diverse real-world environments remains costly and challenging. Action-conditioned world models offer a promising alternative, but they often suffer from limited action controllability and poor generalization to out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. To this end, we present GeniWorld, an interactive world model for robots that generalizes robustly across unseen scenarios. Building on pretrained video generative models, we use URDF-based rendering to transform numerical actions into visual action representations, enabling spatially grounded action control. By explicitly decoupling embodiment kinematics from environmental dynamics, our model mitigates scene overfitting and facilitates modeling of robot-environment interactions. To achieve closed-loop control, we construct an autoregressive video prediction model integrated with high-frequency robot kinematic control, enabling interaction with both robot policies and human teleoperators. In our experiments, even when trained solely on limited fixed-scene data, our model achieves superior in-domain performance and robust zero-shot generalization to highly randomized, unseen environments. For downstream applications, GeniWorld serves as a scalable policy evaluator that remains reliable under environmental perturbations. Furthermore, even with limited real-world demonstrations, GeniWorld generates diverse manipulation trajectories within the world model, improving downstream policy performance and robustness in complex environments.

title: DyPES-VLA: Learning Shared Dynamics Priors and Embodiment-Specific Control for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
summary: DyPES-VLA tackles cross-embodiment manipulation by separating what can be shared across robots from what must stay embodiment-specific: a VLM learns dynamics priors through future prediction over diverse interaction data, while a Mixture-of-Experts action head maps those priors directly into each robot’s native control space. The design avoids manual action-space alignment and uses shared attention plus embodiment-specific feed-forward experts to handle common temporal structure alongside robot-specific kinematics. It reports strong generalist-policy results across simulation and real-world settings, including 98.0% success on LIBERO, 59.25% on RoboCasa-GR1, and 89.02% on RoboTwin 2.0.

extra.full_text: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have become a powerful paradigm for robot manipulation, but training a single generalist policy for heterogeneous robot embodiments remains an open problem. Existing methods have two main limitations. First, they underuse dynamics priors shared across diverse visual and interaction data, limiting cross-embodiment transfer. Second, they require extensive manual preprocessing to convert embodiment-specific actions into a common format. To overcome these limitations, we propose DyPES-VLA, a cross-embodiment VLA that learns shared Dynamics Priors and Embodiment-Specific control. First, we learn shared dynamics priors by training the vision-language model (VLM) with a future-prediction objective on cross-embodiment data, driving the shared query representation to capture object motion, contact, and interaction-induced scene changes. Second, an embodiment-specific Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) action head translates these shared dynamics priors into executable controls directly in each embodiment's native action space, without manually pre-aligning heterogeneous actions into a common format. This head shares attention layers to capture common temporal action structures, while its embodiment-specific feed-forward experts resolve the unique kinematic constraints and control semantics of distinct embodiments. As a generalist policy, our \ourmethod achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-world evaluations, reaching 98.0% success on LIBERO, 59.25% on RoboCasa-GR1, and 89.02% on RoboTwin~2.0.

title: martin-sedlacek/REALM

title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
summary: RRC adapts generative reward models for LLM reinforcement learning by turning their comparative ranking strengths into scalar training signals. It constructs rewards from relative preference rankings using self-competitive ranking among sampled responses and anchor-guided ranking against a small reference set. Across open-ended chat and reasoning benchmarks, this ranking-based reward construction consistently improves RL training over existing ways of deriving rewards from generative reward models.

extra.full_text: Recent advances in reward modeling show a paradigm shift from discriminative reward models to generative reward models. However, despite their strong capabilities in response ranking, generative reward models have not realized their potential in reinforcement learning (RL). Our analysis reveals that this limitation arises from a mismatch between the comparative nature of generative reward modeling and the scalar scoring paradigm adopted by existing RL algorithms. To bridge this gap, we propose a Ranking-based Reward Construction (RRC) approach, which enables generative reward models to provide more effective RL learning signals by deriving rewards from relative preference rankings. RRC introduces two complementary strategies: self-competitive ranking, which exploits comparisons among sampled responses, and anchor-guided ranking, which enables scalable ranking-based reward construction with a small set of reference responses. Experiments across open-ended chat and reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that RRC substantially improves RL training with generative reward models, achieving consistent gains over existing reward construction approaches. Our code can be found at https://github.com/wangclnlp/RRC.

title: Video Friday: Drones Go Heavy in DARPA Lift Challenge
summary: IEEE Spectrum’s Video Friday highlights DARPA’s Lift Challenge, where unconventional heavy-lift drone designs are being tested in a live competition format with recorded livestreams available. The roundup also points to related robot-AI work, including NASA’s SkyFall Mars helicopters carrying flexible fabric-based ground-penetrating radar antennas to search for frozen water, Generalist’s GEN-1 low-level adaptation gains of 10-20x on internal benchmarks, and SonicFly, which lets one UAV follow another using only the leader’s flight sound.

extra.full_text: Video Friday is your weekly selection of awesome robotics videos, collected by your friends at IEEE Spectrum robotics. We also post a weekly calendar of upcoming robotics events for the next few months. Please send us your events for inclusion. Actuate 2026 : 18–19 August 2026, SAN FRANCISCO IROS 2026 : 27 September–1 October 2026, PITTSBURGH Humanoids Summit Seoul : 22–23 September 2026, SEOUL Enjoy today’s videos! The DARPA Lift Challenge is taking place through this weekend. There are a couple of very brief overview videos from the past couple of days, which are only really interesting because they give you a quick look at some utterly bizarre heavy-lift drone designs. If you like what you see, DARPA has recorded livestreams of the entire event so far. We’ve posted one of those at the end of this section, and if you want to be impressed by some super weird drones, check out this and this . [ DARPA Lift Challenge ] When NASA’s SkyFall helicopters take to the Martian skies, one of their tasks will be to hunt for frozen water—a critical resource for future astronauts—using ground-penetrating radar. For that radar to work, the rotorcraft will carry a flexible, fabric-based antenna that extends below the aircraft without interfering with landings or breaking at touchdown. [ NASA ] Why would you even want a five-fingered humanoid hand when you could have something so much better? [ Flexiv ] We’ve improved how GEN-1 learns to adapt to new actuators and new robots at the lowest level, with up to 10-20x gains on internal benchmarks. This significantly boosts performance on high-precision tasks like disassembling parts from a NIST board. [ Generalist ] This is certainly one of the best looking humanoid robots out there. [ Generative Bionics ] A little on the technical side, but the concept here is important, I think: being able to control an assistive robot through touch. [ Tac-Nav ] We present SonicFly, a passive aeroacoustic perception framework that enables one unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to estimate and follow another using only the leader’s intrinsic flight sound. [ General Robotics Lab ] Okay but... Get a job? [ ROBOTIS ]

summary: Hansung Sysco and Robai signed an MOU to test Robai’s general-purpose robot control AI platform, Robot Academy, in rubber and tire manufacturing environments. The collaboration pairs Hansung Sysco’s industrial engineering and smart-factory integration experience with Robai’s robot-control platform to evaluate whether it can be applied and commercialized in real production sites.

title: Regal Rexnord and Fanuc launch integrated linear axis for CRX collaborative robots
summary: Regal Rexnord is partnering with Fanuc on an integrated linear axis for Fanuc CRX collaborative robots, packaging Thomson linear motion hardware with Boston Gear gearheads, Huco couplings, and Kollmorgen motors and software. The result is a more turnkey way to add extended linear travel to CRX cobot deployments, reducing the integration burden for users who need collaborative robots to cover longer work envelopes.

extra.full_text: Regal Rexnord has formed a strategic collaboration with robotics and automation company Fanuc to deliver a fully integrated collaborative robotics solution that combines expertise from many of its brands. title: 리얼월드, 국내 3사와 엔비디아 '아이작' 벤치마크 고도화 나선다
summary: RealWorld is partnering with PhysicsSimLab, SpaceAI, and NdotLight to expand DexBench, a precision dexterity benchmark for humanoid hands being built with NVIDIA. The collaboration will add 3D assets, physics data, and simulation validation around NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena integration, while also feeding improvements into RealWorld’s robot foundation model RLDX-1.

extra.full_text: 리얼월드(대표 류중희)는 국내 시뮬레이션·로보틱스 기업 3사와 업무협약(MOU)을 체결하고, 휴머노이드 정밀 손재주 평가 벤치마크 '덱스벤치(DexBench)' 고도화에 나선다고 7일 밝혔다.리얼월드는 피직스심랩, 스페이스에이아이, 엔닷라이트와 협력해 덱스벤치의 3D 에셋과 물리 데이터, 시뮬레이션 검증 체계를 구축하고, 자체 로봇 파운데이션 모델(RFM) 'RLDX-1'을 고도화할 계획이다.덱스벤치는 리얼월드가 엔비디아와 협력해 수립 중인 평가 벤치마크로 엔비디아의 아이작 랩-아레나 환경과 통합되는 오픈소스 프로젝트로 개발 중이다

title: Brain Corp reports 68 percent growth and surpasses 50,000 autonomous robots worldwide
summary: Brain Corp says its BrainOS-powered robot fleet grew 68% year over year in the first half of 2026 and has now surpassed 50,000 autonomous robots deployed worldwide. The update points to autonomous mobile robots becoming routine operational infrastructure across retail, logistics, airports, commercial cleaning, and inventory management, rather than isolated pilots or niche automation projects.

extra.full_text: Brain Corp, a provider of operating systems for robots, has announced “strong global fleet momentum for the first half of 2026”. title: 한국로봇융합연구원, '2026 제16회 부산로봇경진대회' 8~9일 개최
summary: KIRO is hosting the 16th Busan Robot Competition on August 8-9, 2026, across BEXCO’s second exhibition hall and Tongmyong University’s Marine Robot Hall, with 503 students from 260 teams in Busan, Ulsan, and Gyeongnam. Elementary through university teams will compete in 10 events involving robot building, programming, and AI-based missions, making the event a regional pipeline for hands-on robotics and AI education rather than just a showcase.

title: 로봇카페 라운지엑스24h, 커피값 고공행진에도 할인 운영 확대
summary: 라운지엑스24h가 원두와 인건비 상승으로 커피 프랜차이즈들이 가격을 올리는 흐름과 달리, AI 기반 운영 효율을 바탕으로 할인 운영을 전 매장으로 확대한다. 기존 일부 매장에서 오전 7시 30분부터 오후 2시까지 제공하던 할인 프로모션을 전체 매장에 적용해 출근과 점심 시간대 스페셜티 커피의 가격 접근성을 높이려는 전략이다.

extra.full_text: 최근 원두를 비롯한 주요 원재료 가격과 인건비 상승으로 국내 커피 브랜드들의 가격 인상이 이어지고 있는 가운데 AI 로봇카페 브랜드 라운지엑스24h는 가격을 올리는 대신 할인 운영을 확대하며 상반된 행보를 이어가고 있다. title: AI agents create virtual playgrounds to help robots get crucial training data
summary: MIT researchers built a system that uses three AI agents to assemble realistic 3D indoor scenes from objects, walls, and visual details, creating virtual spaces where robots can rehearse tasks before touching the physical world. The value is in generating richer, more varied training environments so robots can test strategies and collect practice data cheaply and safely, addressing one of the bottlenecks in getting embodied AI to generalize beyond tightly controlled setups.

extra.full_text: A new system developed at MIT uses three agents to piece together the objects, walls, and overall look of a 3D scene. Its realistic recreations of indoor spaces help robots practice skills and try out different ways of doing tasks before they’re powered on. title: 아마존, 영국서 ‘AI 자율 물류’ 현실화…MK30 드론, 12km 반경 배송 상용화
summary: Amazon has begun operating Prime Air drone delivery from its Darlington fulfillment center in England, extending the service beyond the U.S. to real customers in the UK. The system centers on the MK30 drone and ties together AI-based spatial analysis, autonomous flight, real-time obstacle avoidance, weather-data assessment, and warehouse robotics into a more integrated autonomous logistics pipeline, with deliveries reportedly covering a 12 km radius.

title: [게시판] "챗GPT서 포토샵·일러스트 쓴다"...어도비 플러그인 출시 등 단신
summary: Adobe released a plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex that brings more than 70 tools from Adobe Express, Photoshop, Firefly, Illustrator, and related apps into the AI workflow. Users can start creative or editing tasks through the plugin, then continue in Adobe’s own apps when they need finer creative control, advanced editing, or pixel-level precision.

title: Quantum-Inspired Software Shatters Engineering Bottlenecks: BQP and Modovolo Are Rewriting the Aerospace Design Playbook
summary: BQP’s quantum-inspired optimization software is being used by Modovolo to compress aerospace drone design cycles that normally require slow physical iteration. The reported result is faster movement from design exploration to scalable hardware, with Modovolo claiming state-of-the-art drone performance, though the provided text does not give specific benchmarks or technical details on the optimization method.

extra.full_text: Powered by BQP's advanced computing platform, drone manufacturer Modovolo bypasses long design cycles to achieve state-of-the-art performance and scale physical hardware at unprecedented speeds.

title: 서울시립대 기계정보공학과, CJ대한통운 미래기술챌린지 대상 수상
summary: 서울시립대 기계정보공학과 로보틱스 연구실의 UOS-RoboStack 팀이 CJ대한통운 제6회 미래기술챌린지에서 물류 현장 문제를 겨루는 로봇·AI·빅데이터 기술 아이디어로 대상을 받았다. 같은 연구실의 UOS-CCTV 팀도 3위에 올라, 황면중 교수 연구실이 물류 자동화와 현장 지능화 쪽에서 복수의 경쟁력 있는 아이디어를 냈다는 점이 눈에 띈다.

extra.full_text: 서울시립대학교(총장 원용걸) 기계정보공학과 로보틱스 연구실(지도교수 황면중) 소속 ‘UOS-RoboStack’ 팀(석사과정 홍수현, 4학년 김연재, 이유민)이 CJ대한통운이 주관한 ‘제6회 미래기술챌린지’에서 최고상인 대상을 수상했다. 또한 같은 연구실의 ‘UOS-CCTV’ 팀(석사과정 강두인, 조성빈, 최강현)도 3위에 오르는 성과를 거뒀다.올해로 6회째를 맞이한 ‘CJ대한통운 미래기술챌린지’는 물류 로봇, AI, 빅데이터 등 첨단 기술을 활용해 물류 현장의 실질적인 문제를 해결하는 아이디어를 겨루는 국내 대표 물류 기술 경진대회

title: Data center infrastructure company Tate boosts welding productivity 12-fold with fleet of 58 Hirebotics cobots
summary: Tate has rolled out 58 Hirebotics Cobot Welder systems across plants in Arkansas, Virginia, and Kentucky to automate welding for data center infrastructure manufacturing. Hirebotics says the deployment raised per-welder throughput by 12x, suggesting cobot welding is moving from isolated trials into fleet-scale production for high-demand industrial supply chains.

extra.full_text: Hirebotics, a provider of collaborative robot solutions for the metal fabrication industry, has announced that data center infrastructure company Tate, has deployed a fleet of 58 Hirebotics Cobot Welder systems across manufacturing facilities in Arkansas, Virginia and Kentucky.
